pages.text: An intake makes, every tick:$(br2)$(item)RPM x size x size / 40$() mB of air, rounded down.$(br2)$(l)At 256 RPM$()$(li)$(item)1x1$(): 6 mB per tick$(li)$(item)2x2$(): 25 mB per tick$(li)$(item)3x3$(): 57 mB per tick

$(l)At 128 RPM$()$(li)$(item)1x1$(): 3 mB, $(item)2x2$(): 12 mB, $(item)3x3$(): 28 mB per tick$(br2)Because of the rounding, a lone intake makes $(item)nothing below 40 RPM$(). Size counts twice, so a big square is far better than a pile of single intakes at low speed.

A $(item)2x2x5$() blast stove (next pages) uses close to $(item)28 mB of air per tick$(). A 2x2 intake at full speed falls just short of that, so plan a $(item)3x3$() intake, or two 2x2 intakes on the same pipe, for each such stove.$(br2)When nothing pulls the air, the tank simply stays full: an idle intake does no harm.
